tracks.title: Flask on the Step
tracks.subject: a breakfast-radio host who gets up at half past three, and the sleeping wife who leaves a warm flask of tea on the front step for him every morning

tracks.title: The Tent Has Been to Wales
tracks.genre: 70s UK soft-rock with sax hook (10cc and Gerry Rafferty lineage)
tracks.subject: a man who lent his two-man tent to a friend, who lent it to a cousin, and it has now slept nine strangers across three countries while he has never used it

tracks.title: Monday After Closing
tracks.subject: a woman who winds the eleven antique clocks in a small city museum every Monday after closing, and the one clock she leaves stopped at ten past four on purpose

tracks.title: Side B, Eleven Years
tracks.genre: upright-piano saloon torch ballad (1950s late-night lounge)
tracks.subject: a woman who still has the jazz record a man lent her eleven years ago and has never returned it, because as long as she has it he has a reason to call

tracks.title: Back Pew at Half Past Five
tracks.subject: a Finnish church verger who unlocks the church at half past five every winter morning, and the one stranger who always sits in the back pew for ten minutes and never speaks

tracks.title: Tetes Malam untuk Sari
tracks.subject: a young canting hand in a Lasem batik shop drips hot wax on the cloth every time Sari, the cloth-buyer's daughter, walks in, until seven cloths carry the same blot and the owner writes it into his book as the motif Sari Menetes

tracks.title: Telur Dilarang Sampai Jumat
tracks.subject: Asep, a ninth-grader in Tasikmalaya, avoids eggs, bananas and washing his lucky socks all exam week, while Bu Titin at the school-gate warung renames her menu so he can still eat

tracks.title: Soto Jangan Tumpah
tracks.subject: Darto, an ojek driver, takes Rani and her plastic bag of boiling soto home from the corner warung every Thursday at fifteen kilometres an hour, announcing every pothole, and she shares the bowl with him on the kerb

tracks.title: Perca di Atas Meja
tracks.genre: 1960s Melayu film-song orkes with tabla and mandolin
tracks.subject: Bu Nia, a village tailor, sews the leftover scraps of every customer's order into one patchwork cover on her counter, and Pak Hadi keeps asking her to move his red square next to the white lace square of the widow Bu Lastri

tracks.title: Kulkul Pukul Enam
tracks.subject: Pak Wayan, keeper of the banjar's wooden kulkul slit drum, keeps striking six o'clock after the village WhatsApp group replaced him, until children who have never heard it up close ask to try

tracks.title: ドアチャイムのリクエスト
tracks.subject: a convenience-store night clerk and the last wandering nagashi guitarist, who buys one canned coffee at 2 a.m. and pays for it by playing the two-note door chime as a song

tracks.title: 五時のたこ焼き
tracks.genre: Japanese 70s-flavored progressive rock in odd meters (7/8 band song with mellotron)
tracks.subject: after the school festival closes at five, the boy who ran the takoyaki grill hides the last pack under the lid and tries to hand it to the girl who tore 380 tickets alone at the entrance

tracks.title: 梨をかぐ人
tracks.genre: Japanese 1970s southern soul with horn section (Memphis-style, upbeat)
tracks.subject: a shotengai greengrocer whose regular Mrs. Ogawa has sniffed one pear every day for six years without buying, until the day she asks for two

tracks.title: 廃棄のうた
tracks.genre: Japanese forró pop (accordion, zabumba and triangle, upbeat danceable)
tracks.subject: a night clerk who must scan and throw out the expired onigiri at 2 a.m., and says sorry to each one on the senior clerk's enka-style advice to sing the discard with kobushi

tracks.title: ミョウガを買ってきて
tracks.genre: Japanese ukulele cafe folk-pop (bright glockenspiel and brushed snare)
tracks.subject: a newlywed husband sent on his first Sunday errand to buy myoga at the shotengai greengrocer, who has no idea what it looks like

tracks.title: 정남향 구슬
tracks.genre: 1970s Korean group-sound fuzz-guitar rock with Farfisa organ
tracks.subject: a young couple on a jeonse flat-hunting Saturday who set a marble on the floor of each unit to test the slope while the broker keeps repeating that the light is good

tracks.title: 704호 식권
tracks.genre: Korean neoclassical piano and cello duo song in 3/4
tracks.subject: a husband who buys two meal tickets in a hospital cafeteria at visiting hours and eats his lunch while telling his wife in room 704 what the dish tastes like, so she knows what to order when she recovers

tracks.title: 연필로 쓴 길
tracks.subject: a woman hiking Jirisan alone with the guidebook her boyfriend lent her, whose margins are full of his pencil notes, from water warnings to a joke about ramyeon

tracks.title: 약수터 물통
tracks.genre: Korean sin-minyo (new folk song) pop with Casio-style synth and janggu
tracks.subject: a dawn mineral-spring queue where a regular leaves twelve empty jugs to hold his place and goes for breakfast, and a grandmother quietly fills every one of them

tracks.title: 은행 줍는 아침
tracks.genre: Korean freak-folk with autoharp and music box
tracks.subject: a commuter who every October watches an older woman picking ginkgo nuts off the pavement at dawn with long tongs, until one morning she hands him a paper cup of roasted nuts

tracks.title: Kerusi Lebih Satu
tracks.genre: Malay ronggeng band (1930s-style violin-and-accordion dance song)
tracks.subject: Hanim counts the borrowed plastic chairs after a doa selamat kenduri, finds one extra marked in white paint with Zul's name, and keeps miscounting so he has to come and fetch it himself

tracks.title: Sudut Kiri Papan Putih
tracks.genre: 1960s Malay filmi song (Hindustani-influenced Malay film song with sitar and tabla)
tracks.subject: Two tuition-centre teachers share one whiteboard and never meet, so he starts answering her leftover chalk-corner notes in the top left corner she never wipes

tracks.title: Jarum Jala Merah Jambu
tracks.genre: 1960s Malay orkes Melayu (classic accordion-and-suling dance orchestra with gendang)
tracks.subject: Pak Din mends his torn cast net on the jetty with his wife's pink sewing thread because the nylon ran out, and the other fishermen will not stop laughing

tracks.title: Bot Kuning
tracks.genre: Malay 1960s Shadows-style guitar-instrumental pop with sung vocals (twangy lead guitar, spring reverb, upbeat)
tracks.subject: Rahim scrapes his old hull and paints it bright yellow among sixty identical blue boats so his wife can pick his boat out from the kitchen window when he comes home

tracks.title: Butang Kedua
tracks.genre: Malay zapin acoustic ballad (gambus/oud, marwas, accordion, steady 4/4 zapin rhythm)
tracks.subject: A Johor wife sews back the second button on her husband's shirt every Sunday before he crosses the Causeway for work in Singapore, and it always comes loose by Wednesday

tracks.title: 燒豆腐 Sio tāu-hū
tracks.subject: A stone-mill tofu maker grinds beans from 3 a.m. and leaves the first warm block wrapped in cloth on a quiet woman's windowsill; each day she returns the cloth folded square, and finally a note.

tracks.title: 漏氣 Làu-khuì
tracks.genre: Taigi smoky torch-song jazz with muted trumpet
tracks.subject: A woman who runs a bicycle-repair shop beside a temple dips the same customer's back-tyre tube in the water basin every Tuesday and realises the single pinhole is made by his own pin; she patches it slowly anyway.

tracks.title: 手尺麵線 Tshiú-tshioh mī-suànn
tracks.genre: Taigi 1970s dance-hall twist pop with horn riffs
tracks.subject: A mee-sua noodle maker measures every bundle by his own outstretched arms until his new wife, whose arms are shorter, makes shorter bundles, and the customers start queuing for hers because the short strands cook faster.

tracks.title: 菜瓜衫 Tshài-kue-sann
tracks.genre: Taigi Appalachian-style old-time clawhammer banjo folk
tracks.subject: A grandmother sews a little bag from each grandchild's outgrown shirt to cover every young loofah on her trellis against fruit flies, so the garden ends up wearing the whole family.

tracks.title: 賰三秒 Tshun sann-bió
tracks.subject: A woman who always steps off the kerb with exactly three seconds left on the pedestrian green-man countdown mistimes it once, and the man waiting at the corner holds up his hand to stop a scooter for her.

tracks.title: เก้าอี้หายไปหนึ่งตัว
tracks.genre: 1950s-style early luk thung with Hawaiian steel guitar and saxophone
tracks.subject: a man who rents out 150 plastic chairs for the temple-fair film night counts them at dawn, finds one missing, and traces it to a sleeping old man who carried it off to nap

tracks.title: ชื่อปักผิดทั้งโรงเรียน
tracks.genre: Isan lam sarawan couple-dance song with khaen and electric phin
tracks.subject: a Grade 9 girl whose name was embroidered wrong on her new uniform shirt (Nongnam as Nongnum), until the whole school and even the headmaster call her by the typo

tracks.title: เซียมซีเบอร์เดิม
tracks.genre: Thai pastoral chamber-folk in 3/4 with clarinet and harmonium
tracks.subject: a woman shakes the fortune sticks at a shrine every month and always draws number 28, and the shy man who sells joss sticks there slips her a different slip every time

tracks.title: เก้าอี้ตัวเตี้ยข้างประตู
tracks.genre: 1980s Thai orchestral luk krung ballad with harp, cello and oboe
tracks.subject: the owner of a bus-stop shop keeps a low stool by the door for a regular, a woman walking slowly after hip surgery, and starts timing his tea refills to her pace

tracks.title: โน้ตแปะจอ
tracks.genre: Thai vibraphone boogie-pop with slap bass and Rhodes
tracks.subject: two office workers share one hot desk on opposite days and leave increasingly flirty sticky notes on the shared monitor without ever meeting

tracks.title: Đinh Trong Lốp
tracks.genre: Vietnamese nhạc sến slow rock with Hammond organ
tracks.subject: a young sidewalk motorbike repairman under a tamarind tree and a woman who keeps wheeling in flat tyres, until the day her tyre is fine and she comes anyway

tracks.title: Giọt Phin Thứ Chín
tracks.subject: a clerk in a Saigon cafe who stares at a slow coffee phin and begs each drip to hurry, because his boss's clock is ticking and the phin takes its own time

tracks.title: Rau Răm Trong Chai Nhựa
tracks.genre: Vietnamese twee indie pop with glockenspiel and ukulele
tracks.subject: a girl who carries cuttings of her grandmother's rau răm and basil in cut plastic bottles to her sixth-floor apartment balcony and phones grandma every morning to report the leaf count

tracks.title: Bảng Giá Chú Sáu
tracks.subject: a sidewalk shoe-mender whose cardboard price list has not changed since 2009, and who sings it out to every customer who asks him to raise it

tracks.title: Gấu Quần Anh
tracks.genre: Vietnamese flamenco-pop (rumba flamenca) with nylon guitar, palmas and cajon
tracks.subject: a sidewalk tailor's daughter hurriedly hemming a young man's trousers at her sewing-machine stall before his job interview, biting the thread, having already measured him by eye for months

tracks.title: 熱奶茶，走甜
tracks.subject: a cha chaan teng waiter who has written the same order slip for a regular at table seven for three years without a word between them, until she orders in his kitchen shorthand and adds one more item

tracks.title: 一碗苦茶
tracks.genre: Cantonese opera-film song pop with small band (siu kuk tune, gaohu and yangqin)
tracks.subject: a young man who orders a bowl of the bitterest twenty-four-herb tea every day at a herbal tea shop just to keep talking to the girl at the counter, until she tells him to stop drinking and shares a honey tea instead

tracks.title: 平路返屋企
tracks.subject: a woman in brand-new heels who draws a stair-free route by hand to her own birthday dinner on a hill, detours through six landmarks, and arrives by the kitchen back door where her friends are hiding the cake

tracks.title: 唔洗得
tracks.genre: Cantonese mandolin and melodica street-folk pop
tracks.subject: a cha chaan teng tea master who refuses to wash the dark tea-straining sock he has used for twenty years, and the hygiene inspector who arrives on the busiest morning

tracks.title: 一百粒奶糖
tracks.subject: a man who hands his girlfriend one milk candy at her door every night instead of saying what he feels, while she saves every wrapper in a biscuit tin until it holds one hundred and she counts them out and answers

tracks.title: 第七張稿紙
tracks.genre: 1990s Taipei string-section slow-dance ballad (harp, cello and string quartet)
tracks.subject: a young man who has copied the same love letter onto seven sheets of grid manuscript paper because every draft gets one ink blot at the word for 'like', and finally slides the seventh under the third-floor neighbour's door, where she has been doing the same

tracks.title: 還差一個宋江
tracks.genre: Mandarin melodica-and-fingerpicking small-town minjian folk (民謠)
tracks.subject: a man in his late thirties who still keeps a biscuit tin of 107 instant-noodle collector cards from his school years, missing only the 'Song Jiang' card he swapped away at the playground in 1998, and at the class reunion the classmate pulls the worn card from his wallet

tracks.title: 七號請進
tracks.genre: Mandarin 1960s exotica lounge (vibraphone, bongos and flute)
tracks.subject: six patients in a Chinese-medicine clinic waiting room who all stand up because the number machine jammed and printed ticket number seven six times, while the teapot steams and the nurse calls 'number seven' again

tracks.title: 簽得太漂亮
tracks.genre: 1980s boogie-funk with horn stabs (slap bass, synth bass and brass section)
tracks.subject: a fifth-grader in Taipei who forges his mother's signature in the school contact book after a bad quiz, practises it thirty times, adds a little heart, and is caught because his mother always signs with a smiley face

tracks.title: 最後一支原子筆
tracks.genre: Taiwanese jangle-pop indie rock (12-string guitar, organ and tambourine)
tracks.subject: a woman keeps a tin of ballpoint pens taken from every place she and her boyfriend visited, and when the Hualien motel pen dries up and goes in the drawer, he secretly picks it apart at night and refits a new refill

tracks.title: Saturday Jar
tracks.genre: Hawaiian slack-key and steel-guitar ballad (island pop, 1970s Gabby Pahinui lineage)
tracks.subject: a honey seller at a Saturday farmers' table who writes a new line on the label of one jar for the same woman every week, and she buys only one jar, so he has shelves of unsent lines at home

tracks.title: Six Weeks Behind
tracks.genre: psychedelic folk (Incredible String Band lineage, acoustic, droney)
tracks.subject: two pen pals since age eleven, one on Orkney and one in Tasmania, whose letters take six weeks each way so each answers a question the other asked in another season

tracks.title: Dear Tommy, Love Me
tracks.genre: 1960s French yé-yé pop sung in English (Farfisa organ, jangling guitar, tambourine, girlish lead)
tracks.subject: a girl who ghostwrites her best friend's love notes to a boy, and the boy's replies keep describing details only she wrote, so she's the one falling for him

tracks.title: Mouthing It at the Back
tracks.genre: Scottish ceilidh folk-rock (accordion and fiddle with a full rock backline, Waterboys and Runrig lineage)
tracks.subject: a minister's speechwriter stands at the back of the hall mouthing every line, then the minister drops her best pun, and she mouths the rest into the silence

tracks.title: Bees in the Sousaphone
tracks.genre: traditional New Orleans Dixieland jazz (collective improvisation, cornet, clarinet, trombone, banjo, tuba)
tracks.subject: a swarm of bees settles in the bell of the sousaphone the morning before the parade, and the beekeeper must be coaxed away from his honey stand to talk them out while the band keeps time

tracks.title: Wajan Retak di Bulan Ini
tracks.subject: an old pandai besi in Kampung Tugu reforges the same widow's cracked frying pan every month, and slowly understands she cracks it on purpose to keep coming back to his forge

tracks.title: Kursi Kesembilan
tracks.genre: Javanese gending pop with siter and kendang ciblon
tracks.subject: a travelling pasar-malam acrobat balances on a tower of nine chairs on her husband's shoulders, and he secretly recites the shopping list to stay steady, so she ends up with the whole list in her head

tracks.title: Sandi Pukul Sembilan
tracks.subject: a wife in Pariaman and her husband working in Medan talk every night at nine on a ham radio rig, so the whole street listens, and they speak only in Minang proverbs so the neighbours cannot follow

tracks.title: Ban Bocor Lagi, Neng?
tracks.genre: Sundanese degung pop with suling and kendang
tracks.subject: a tukang tambal ban on a Lembang road patches the same girl's bicycle tyre every Saturday, and finds the puncture is always a neat pin hole, so he starts hiding a pin box and then hands her the last patch

tracks.title: Sebelum Pukul Sepuluh
tracks.subject: a wartel operator counts down to ten o'clock, when the night tariff starts, while a student in the booth waits with his girlfriend's number and coins, and she lets him wait until the very last minute

tracks.title: CQ、こちら石垣
tracks.genre: Yaeyama-style Ryukyu folk-pop with sanshin and sanba (kachashi-lilt, Yaeyama island duet feel)
tracks.subject: an Ishigaki man on his roof every night at ten calling CQ on his ham radio to a woman in Hokkaido, who answers with her snowy weather while he reports 28 degrees and cicadas, until she is the first to say they should meet

tracks.title: ひまわり食堂の黄色
tracks.genre: Showa-era orchestral kayokyoku (1960s grand-orchestra TV-show ballad, strings and harp)
tracks.subject: a hand-lettering signboard painter who repaints the faded yellow sunflower on a widow's diner sign every April for twelve years, still coming this year when the paint has not faded, and she says come again next year

tracks.title: ぼくのカエルは帽子になった
tracks.genre: 1980s Japanese electro-funk boogie (Tokyo studio-session boogie, slap bass and Linn-style drum machine)
tracks.subject: a 38-year-old father at a Sunday community-centre origami class whose teacher is a seven-year-old champion named Mio, and whose paper frog keeps turning out as a hat

tracks.title: 七番席のお客さん
tracks.genre: Japanese Taisho-roman dark cabaret ballad (accordion, felt piano and clarinet, silent-film hall atmosphere)
tracks.subject: a young woman benshi narrating a silent film in an Asakusa-style hall to the one customer in seat seven, an old man who never watches the screen, only her mouth, so she slows every line to his reading speed

tracks.title: チラシの端っこ
tracks.genre: Japanese busking-duo folk-pop (harmonica, twelve-string guitar and cajon, 2000s street-duo feel)
tracks.subject: a woman who finds a hand-written note in the margin of the same pizza-shop flyer in her mailbox every Thursday, never orders, and one week finally writes back in the margin with her order

tracks.title: 인형이 대신 말해요
tracks.subject: a ventriloquist at a Daegu shopping-street stage who is too shy to speak to the bakery woman, so his wooden dummy blurts out his feelings and he has to pretend it is not him

tracks.title: 활터의 빈 과녁
tracks.genre: 1970s Korean Sanullim-style folk-rock with harmonium and flute
tracks.subject: a woman in her first year at a traditional Korean archery range (gungdo) whose arrows keep landing in the sand in front of the target, until the old range master tells her to stop aiming and breathe out like a sigh

tracks.title: 눈 내리는 유리 속
tracks.genre: Korean indie-folk with accordion, stomp-clap and mandolin
tracks.subject: a woman who repairs snow globes in a tiny Euljiro shop, and a quiet man who keeps bringing back the same Namsan Tower globe for a leak that she realizes he is making himself so he can see her

tracks.title: 뒤집힌 카드 한 장
tracks.genre: Korean bolero trio ballad with requinto guitar and bongos
tracks.subject: a tarot reader at a Hongdae folding table whose regular, a quiet man who comes every Thursday, always draws the same card, until she stops reading the cards and asks him out

tracks.title: 산장 방명록
tracks.genre: Korean Celtic-folk slow air with uilleann pipes, fiddle and bodhran
tracks.subject: a mountain-hut caretaker on Jirisan who keeps a lamp lit every night and reads a hiker's yearly guestbook line, and the one winter the hiker writes just the word 'I'm back'

tracks.title: Manik Skor Ke Tujuh
tracks.subject: a girl who keeps score on the bead rack at a Seremban snooker hall and slides one bead too many for the quiet boy at table four

tracks.title: Jeruk Kedondong Pukul Dua
tracks.genre: Zapin Johor with gambus (acoustic gambus-and-marwas dance song)
tracks.subject: a husband in Muar sent out at 2 a.m. for jeruk kedondong for his craving wife, knocking on the pickle-lady's door and ending up helping her stir the jar

tracks.title: Loceng Basikal Mak Bidan
tracks.genre: Kristang branyo (Portuguese Settlement Melaka folk dance song)
tracks.subject: an old bidan in the Melaka Portuguese Settlement who cycles to every birth and is paid only in kuih, so her pantry now holds forty-one tins

tracks.title: Pantun dalam Songkok
tracks.genre: Perak dendang with rebab (slow Malay folk song with rebab, gong and gendang)
tracks.subject: a wife in Kuala Kangsar ironing her husband's songkok before Friday prayers finds a pantun he wrote for her thirty years ago folded in the lining

tracks.title: Cincin di Poket Hujung
tracks.subject: the dawn cleaner of a Klang snooker hall who finds an engagement ring in a corner pocket and puts up a notice, and the woman who comes to claim it asks him to keep it there

tracks.title: 十二聲 Tsap-jī siann
tracks.subject: A Tamsui church bell-ringer who must pull exactly twelve strokes at noon loses count every day because the florist across the street waves from her window, so the congregation files out for lunch two strokes early.

tracks.title: 骨牌少一塊 Kut-pâi tsió tsit-tè
tracks.genre: Taigi 1990s Hokkien power ballad with sax solo
tracks.subject: Four old friends play 32-tile tin-gau domino at a Lukang temple courtyard table and have used a bottle cap for the missing tile for twenty years, until the carpenter among them carves a replacement from an ebony chopstick.

tracks.title: 倒寫的名 Tò-siá ê miâ
tracks.subject: A seal-carver's apprentice must carve his girlfriend Huē-bûn's name in mirror writing and has ruined ninety-nine stones, so on the hundredth he presses it first on his own palm.

tracks.title: 媒人喙糊瘰瘰 Muê-lâng-tshuì hôo-lui-lui
tracks.subject: A village matchmaker tells the groom's family that the girl eats very little and the girl's family that the boy hardly talks, then at the first meeting he talks nonstop and she eats nonstop and they suit perfectly.

tracks.title: 旋轉門 Suān-tsuân-mn̂g
tracks.subject: A white-gloved hotel doorman in Taipei counts one-two-three for every turn of the revolving door, and a woman in a green skirt who takes it twice every Thursday afternoon never says why.

tracks.title: พี่เลี้ยงบ้านเฮา
tracks.genre: Isan lam ruang story-lam dance song (group-lam band, fast storytelling groove)
tracks.subject: Noi, a Roi Et nanny in a Bangkok townhouse, has taught three-year-old Ton to say 'saep nua' at the dinner table, and at his school recital he says it into the microphone while his mother turns pale

tracks.title: ปลาไม่กินเบ็ด
tracks.genre: 1980s Thai hard-rock sing-along with Thai-scale riffs and shouted chorus (big-guitar pub rock)
tracks.subject: Uncle Daeng sits at the same canal bank every Sunday and has hooked only one rubber sandal, which he now brings home and lines up beside the other 'catches' on his shelf

tracks.title: ก้าวคู่ที่สวนลุม
tracks.genre: Thai slow jazz-blues (12-bar minor blues with Hammond organ and muted trumpet)
tracks.subject: A woman in her fifties at the dawn tai chi circle in Lumphini Park has been copying the slow moves of the man opposite her for a year, and today he turns up beside her and they finish the form in step

tracks.title: แจ็กเก็ตยีนส์ตัวนั้น
tracks.genre: Thai trip-hop (dusty breakbeat, Rhodes and cello, late-night downtempo)
tracks.subject: Nit, browsing a Chatuchak second-hand stall, pulls a denim jacket off the rack and finds in the pocket a folded note in the handwriting of the best friend she stopped speaking to three years ago

tracks.title: ผ้าปะหนังตะลุง
tracks.genre: Southern Thai nang talung shadow-theatre song (rhythmic nora-style percussion, sung narration)
tracks.subject: A nang talung puppeteer in Phatthalung burns a hole in his clown puppet Nai Theng the night before a school fair, patches it with a pink sweet wrapper, and the whole screen glows pink to the children's delight

tracks.title: Dưới tấm nỉ xanh
tracks.genre: Tây Nguyên cồng chiêng folk-pop with k'ni fiddle
tracks.subject: Anh Khôi, who re-covers the green felt of the pool tables in a Buôn Ma Thuột hall each year, finds something small under the old cloth every time and keeps a box of them for the owner's daughter

tracks.title: Bậc đá mòn
tracks.genre: Hát văn ritual chamber folk (đàn nguyệt, phách, trống chầu)
tracks.subject: Bà Tư, a stonemason in the Ninh Vân quarry, recuts the worn steps of a mountain temple and carves one step with a shallow dip where an old woman's walking stick always lands

tracks.title: Người tượng biết nói
tracks.genre: 2010s Vietnamese indie folk with banjo and harmonica
tracks.subject: A silver-painted street mime on a Hội An bridge who cannot speak while in costume proposes to his girlfriend using only gestures, and she has to guess the question

tracks.title: Màu cho em
tracks.genre: 1980s Vietnamese overseas synth-ballad (DX7 pads and drum machine)
tracks.subject: A hand-tinting photo colourist in a Sài Gòn shop who has coloured one woman's black-and-white portrait every week for a year and keeps getting her lipstick colour slightly wrong on purpose, to make her come back and correct him

tracks.title: Chị bán vé đọc kết phim
tracks.genre: Vietnamese Boston-waltz nhạc vàng (3/4 accordion-and-guitar dance song)
tracks.subject: A small-town cinema ticket seller in Cần Thơ who cannot stop telling the queue how each film ends, so the audience now buys tickets just to hear her ending first and then watches the film anyway

tracks.title: 慢咗三分鐘
tracks.genre: Cantonese 1980s sophisti-pop (Rhodes, fretless bass, light synth)
tracks.subject: A Sheung Wan watch repairer whose regular customer brings in the same watch each month saying it runs three minutes slow; nothing is wrong with it and he keeps pretending to fix it so she keeps coming

tracks.title: 十一個聽眾
tracks.genre: Cantonese bangzi-style folk-opera pop (banhu, gongs, wooden clappers)
tracks.subject: A young woman records her podcast inside a wardrobe with towels for soundproofing; she has exactly eleven listeners, all relatives, whom she thanks by name each episode, until episode forty shows a twelfth, a stranger in Canada

tracks.title: 接機牌
tracks.genre: Cantonese West Coast cool-jazz saxophone ballad
tracks.subject: Two pen pals matched by a school scheme at twelve finally meet at Hong Kong airport arrivals at fifty, each holding a card written in the other's handwriting

tracks.title: 晨運佬
tracks.genre: Cantonese 2000s minimal-funk R&B (Neptunes-style sparse drum machine, clavinet, falsetto)
tracks.subject: A man who fancies the woman leading the six a.m. tai chi group in Victoria Park joins in a hoodie, bad at every move, and is gently corrected each morning until he is the one who stays to tidy the chairs

tracks.title: 星期五澆水
tracks.subject: After her desk neighbour resigned, a woman keeps watering the small cactus he left behind every Friday and leaves him progress notes in his old tray, hoping he will come back to collect it

tracks.title: 酸菜罈子蓋
tracks.subject: a young man carries his own three-year-old jar of pickled mustard greens to his girlfriend's flat to cook for her, and the lid will not open for him, her roommate or her brother, until she taps it once with a spoon handle

tracks.title: 舊書店的鉛筆字
tracks.subject: the owner of a tiny second-hand bookshop writes each price in pencil on the inside cover, and one Saturday buys back a novel from a woman who sold it to him last spring, finding a pressed ticket stub in it that is now his to keep or return

tracks.title: 公園裡的小板凳
tracks.genre: Mandarin Irish folk session (fiddle and tin whistle)
tracks.subject: a matchmaking auntie in a city park carries forty paper resumes, notices two of her clients, a bus mechanic and a pharmacist, both walk the same path at six every morning, and quietly moves her folding stool until they have to sit beside each other

tracks.title: 送報的檸檬
tracks.subject: a woman who delivers newspapers by bicycle before dawn down one Tainan lane folds each paper differently for a retired teacher, who hangs one lemon on the gatepost every Friday, and she has been counting the lemons

tracks.title: 論文要訂好
tracks.subject: a bookbinder is handed a hundred-page doctoral thesis at midnight that must be bound and on a desk by nine, and he cannot stop reading the dedication page, which names the student's cleaning-lady mother

tracks.title: Counter Number Three
tracks.subject: A middle-aged man named Mr. Odell buys a bottle of vitamin C he does not need every Thursday at the same pharmacy counter just to hear the pharmacist, Bernadette, say hello; after eleven bottles she writes her phone number on the receipt.

tracks.title: Odd Days, Even Days
tracks.subject: Sixty-year-old identical twin brothers own one old bicycle between them and ride it on alternate dates, odd days for one and even days for the other, until the 31st of the month starts an argument.

tracks.title: False Bottom
tracks.genre: Canterbury-scene jazz-rock pop (Soft Machine and Caravan lineage)
tracks.subject: A stage magician's assistant who spends every show folded into the false bottom of a trunk, counting the audience's applause from inside, decides tonight that she will take the bow before him, because the trick only works on her cue.

tracks.title: Fresh Paste Friday
tracks.genre: UK freakbeat (1966-67 mod and psychedelic beat)
tracks.subject: A bill-poster pastes gig posters onto the same hoarding by the bus station every Friday morning and finds each one peeled off by Monday, so he starts printing an extra copy for the girl who clearly wants it on her bedroom wall.

tracks.title: Quarter Past Twelve in Almeria
tracks.subject: A stunt gunfighter at a tourist western town in the Almería desert has been shot dead at the same balcony every day at 12:15 for twenty-two years; today a small child in the crowd claps for him alone.

tracks.title: Hidung Bang Mamat
tracks.genre: Betawi samrah pop (harmonium, gambus and marwas)
tracks.subject: A Betawi man whose nose has been blocked since August buys perfume for his girlfriend by making the Blok M shop assistant describe every bottle, then finds the words he borrowed are exactly what she smells

tracks.title: Kartu di Kantong Belakang
tracks.genre: Toba Batak hasapi folk-pop (hasapi, sulim and garantung)
tracks.subject: In Balige a woman buys a secondhand library book at a clearance sale and finds the same borrower's name on the due-date card of every book she picks, so she starts borrowing everything he borrowed and slips a note into the last card

tracks.title: Kartu Hak Milik
tracks.subject: A Medan man who has lost every game of Monopoli to his younger sister for twenty years hides a stolen property card in his sock for the rematch, then sees three cards fall out of her sock too

tracks.title: Kuda Berhenti di Rumah Itu
tracks.genre: Lombok Sasak cilokaq pop (gambus, suling and rebana)
tracks.subject: A cidomo horse-cart driver in Mataram whose horse Si Hitam stops dead at one gate every morning because the girl inside feeds him sugarcane, until the driver tells his passenger to get out because they have arrived

tracks.title: Botol Melati
tracks.subject: A rig worker's wife in Balikpapan soaks jasmine from the back fence in oil before every 28-day rotation and refills the small bottle in his jacket pocket so his collar smells of home

tracks.title: りんごは十円玉の大きさ
tracks.genre: Tohoku minyo-pop (Tsugaru jonkara-bushi feel, shamisen with taiko)
tracks.subject: A nervous office worker in a Hirosaki tattoo studio asks an old woman tattooist for an apple the size of a 100-yen coin on his forearm, and she counts the needle pricks to a shamisen beat to keep him from flinching

tracks.title: 最後の日に言えた一言
tracks.genre: Japanese 70s New Music folk-rock (Fukuoka four-piece band feel)
tracks.subject: A Japanese interpreter who has translated a visiting Thai engineer's every sentence for a week at a Hakata factory falls in love; on his last day he says one clumsy Japanese sentence that she does not have to translate

tracks.title: フィルムが替わる八秒前
tracks.genre: Japanese 1980s technopop (YMO-style synth pop with drum machine)
tracks.subject: A projectionist in a thirty-seat Koenji cinema counts down to the reel changeover by watching the cue dots; tonight his girlfriend in row F catches his eye and he misses the switch, leaving the screen white for eight seconds

tracks.title: 鉛筆の返事
tracks.genre: Japanese slowcore (sparse guitar and brushed drums, low-tempo band)
tracks.subject: A clerk at a small used-record shop in Koenji finds faint pencil notes from one previous owner on every sleeve in a box she is pricing, and starts answering in pencil before selling each one

tracks.title: B面に替わる前に
tracks.genre: Showa jazz-kissa hard bop quartet song (Japanese vocal over a live quartet)
tracks.subject: A salaryman's lunch hour at a jazz kissa is exactly one LP side; today the old master leaves the record on side A so he stays ten minutes longer, and the boss walks in to find him sitting there

tracks.title: 보고 싶다를 먼저 배운 날
tracks.subject: A Seoul office worker and her Colombian language-exchange partner meet every Tuesday in a cafe corner; the first Korean phrase he learned was 'I miss you', and he now says it at all the wrong moments

tracks.title: 열쇠는 하나뿐이에요
tracks.subject: A neighbourhood locksmith cuts a tiny key for a seven-year-old's diary padlock, and the girl insists there may be only one key, so he must refuse to make a spare

tracks.title: 아이스께끼 트위스트
tracks.genre: 1960s Korean US-army-club twist and go-go rock and roll
tracks.subject: A teenage ice-lolly (aiseukkeki) seller outside a 1965 US-army-club gate in Dongducheon whose cooler box leaks, so he twists in place to sell out before the ice melts

tracks.title: 포대기는 어려워
tracks.genre: Korean samulnori percussion pop (kkwaenggwari, janggu, buk and sogo with a bright electric bass; clearly sung)
tracks.subject: A first-time father on a video call with his mother-in-law, trying to swaddle his newborn with a bath towel and getting it wrong four times

tracks.title: 노아 인형이 없어졌어요
tracks.subject: A Sunday-school teacher who lost the felt Noah cutout before the lesson improvises with one of her own socks, and the children vote it the best Noah yet

tracks.title: Hitam Dalam Asap
tracks.genre: Malay mak yong court ensemble song (Kelantan rebab, serunai and gong)
tracks.subject: A young Labu Sayong potter in Kuala Kangsar stays up all night feeding rice husk to the smoke-firing pit that turns the pots black, and hides a note in the base of the smallest pot for the city girl who bought it.

tracks.title: Lelaki Tinggi Segak
tracks.genre: Malay bangsawan theatre song (1920s Malay stage operetta with violin and clarinet)
tracks.subject: A palm reader under a rain tree beside an old theatre who tells every customer the same line about a tall handsome stranger, until a tall man in a white suit sits down and she has no line left.

tracks.title: Pin Perak Lima Puluh
tracks.genre: Malay symphonic progressive rock (1970s Mellotron-and-organ prog)
tracks.subject: A retired railway signalman in Kuala Lipis who has given blood every four months for thirteen years is about to receive the silver pin for his fiftieth donation and wonders who carries it.

tracks.title: Kuda Tak Mahu Jalan
tracks.genre: Bajau dalling-dalling (Sabah west-coast gambus and tambourine dance song)
tracks.subject: A Bajau boy in Kota Belud grooming his pony Si Merah for the horsemen's parade, who finds the pony only trots when someone sings the dalling-dalling, so he must sing the whole parade route.

tracks.title: Harmonium Tak Rosak
tracks.genre: Malay qawwali-style devotional-romantic song (harmonium, tabla and handclap call-and-response)
tracks.subject: A harmonium repairer in Brickfields who finds nothing wrong with the old family harmonium the same girl brings in every month, and finally stops pretending to search for the fault.

tracks.title: 三〇七號房 Sann-lîng-tshit hō-pâng
tracks.subject: A day-shift hotel receptionist in Taichung has quietly kept room 307 for a regular Tuesday salesman for a year, writes his name in the register, and finally decides to give him hers.

tracks.title: 字模盤 Jī-bôo-puânn
tracks.subject: In 1985 a Tainan trading-company typist, working a Chinese typewriter with a 2,500-character tray, keeps slipping her boyfriend's character into the contracts, until he turns up and mistypes the word for love.

tracks.title: 紙條仔的字 Tsuá-tiâu-á ê jī
tracks.genre: Taigi West Coast cool-jazz chamber ballad
tracks.subject: A Taipei taxi driver keeps a tin box of the scrap-paper addresses passengers scribbled, reads each handwriting like a face, and one night a young man hands him a slip that only says take me home.

tracks.title: 粉筆寫的聖詩 Hún-pit siá ê sèng-si
tracks.genre: Taigi Presbyterian four-part hymn with pump organ
tracks.subject: A fourteen-year-old who letters the hymn numbers on the chalkboard in a Tainan Presbyterian church smudges a 3 into an 8 one Sunday, so half the congregation sings two different hymns at once.

tracks.title: 皮箱的貼紙 Phuê-siunn ê thiap-tsóa
tracks.subject: A young bellboy at a Sun Moon Lake hotel guesses each guest's hometown from the stickers on their suitcase, until a woman's first sticker turns out to be his own village railway station.

tracks.title: สามสิบสอง
tracks.genre: Lanna sueng-and-salo acoustic pop (Chiang Mai string-ensemble style)
tracks.subject: In a Lampang cloth shop, tailor Pa Noi measures old Lung Chan, who sucks in his belly every year, and quietly writes 32 in her notebook while leaving extra seam allowance for his real waist.

tracks.title: ร่มสิบเอ็ดคัน
tracks.genre: Thai 1990s new jack swing pop (Grammy-era dance-pop)
tracks.subject: A reception clerk in a Bangkok office keeps the umbrella that Nok forgets by his desk every Friday, now has eleven in his steel locker, and finally leaves one on her desk with a note.

tracks.title: ช่องเก้าแนวนอน
tracks.genre: Thai khrueang sai chamber pop (saw duang, khim and khlui)
tracks.mood: tender, quietly funny, slow morning warmth
tracks.subject: Every Sunday morning a retired husband secretly pencils wrong answers into the Thai crossword his wife fills in with a black pen, just so she will look up and scold him.

tracks.title: ปกเสื้อแข็ง
tracks.genre: Bangkok 1970s Philly-style string soul (Thai vintage soul)
tracks.subject: Jeh Lek irons office shirts for five baht each at a Silom alley stall and reads her customers from their collars: heavy starch means interview tomorrow, no starch means no sleep.

tracks.title: กระดิ่งคนลับมีด
tracks.genre: Bangkok ballroom cha-cha-chá orchestra song (1950s Latin dance orchestra)
tracks.subject: Every Wednesday old knife-grinder Lung Thong rings his bicycle bell down a Thonburi alley where nobody answers except Fon, age seven, who brings the same butter knife to be sharpened.

tracks.title: Diều Sáo Đồi Chè
tracks.genre: Phu Tho hat gheo folk-pop (flirtatious call-and-response, bamboo flute and dan nhi)
tracks.subject: A Phú Thọ tea-picker's son flies a paper kite fitted with a bamboo flute so it hums over the tea hills; the girl picking on the next hill ties a red scarf to her own kite tail and tugs back, until the two strings tangle.

tracks.title: Ba Cái Áo Khoác
tracks.subject: At the Tân Sơn Nhất check-in counter, Hạnh's bag weighs 26 kg against a 23 kg limit, so she strips off the three coats she wore to dodge the fee and twists through the queue handing out coconut candy, while her mother's jar of fish paste stays in.

tracks.title: Ngai Vàng Chiều Nay
tracks.genre: Hue nhac cung dinh court-ensemble pop ballad (nha nhac colour)
tracks.subject: A veteran wedding photographer in Huế who has shot forty years of couples in royal costume before the Thái Hòa palace finally persuades his wife, who brought his cơm hến lunch, to sit on the throne chair in a borrowed yellow áo dài so he can photograph her once.

tracks.title: Cầu Khỉ Hai Tay Vịn
tracks.genre: Nam Bo ly folk ballad with guitar phim lom (Mekong)
tracks.subject: In a Vĩnh Long hamlet a girl is too scared to cross the one-log monkey bridge to her mother's house, and a young man who passes each evening says nothing but ties a bamboo handrail a little longer every day until she steps onto it.

tracks.title: Nhầm Vali Đêm Nội Bài
tracks.subject: At the Nội Bài baggage carousel after midnight a man takes home the wrong black suitcase; inside are an orange sweater and a notebook with a phone number, and the woman who took his bag has found his harmonica, so they arrange to swap at the counter.

tracks.title: 帶件褸啦
tracks.subject: A late-evening radio weather-reader in Kowloon ends every forecast with 'bring a jacket' for one lone taxi-driver listener, until a man in a worn jacket turns up at the studio door.

tracks.title: 樁
tracks.genre: Cantonese Guangdong music chamber folk (gaohu and yangqin)
tracks.subject: A land surveyor knocks a boundary peg into a hillside path, and every morning an old woman moves it three feet so her bench stays outside the works fence.

tracks.title: 無名嗰條巷
tracks.genre: Cantonese Dixieland jazz band (clarinet, trombone, cornet, banjo, tuba, washboard)
tracks.subject: A city map-maker names every lane on a new street map but leaves one tiny lane blank and pins it for the woman he first met there.

tracks.title: 冇事發生
tracks.subject: A night watchman at a Kwun Tong ice factory writes 'nothing happened' in the logbook, then starts inventing ever wilder entries to stay awake, until the day supervisor reads them aloud.

tracks.title: 阿嫲話唔使帶遮
tracks.genre: Cantonese 1960s girl-group pop (Brill Building style: tambourine, jangly guitar, upright bass, handclaps, strings)
tracks.subject: A TV weather presenter whose grandmother phones the studio during the 6:55 forecast to overrule him by what she reads from the clouds above her washing line.

tracks.title: 最後一球灰藍線
tracks.subject: two strangers reach on a Saturday for the very last ball of grey-blue wool of the same dye lot in a Beipu wool shop; the shop auntie winds it into two balls so they each knit half, and the two scarves match

tracks.title: 卡帶轉啊轉
tracks.subject: a long-haul truck driver on the Sichuan-Tibet highway whose only cassette was chewed by the deck, winds it back with a pencil at every rest stop, and now the song wobbles and he sings along with the wobble

tracks.title: 我的底片有你的手指
tracks.subject: a young man develops the roll from the old film camera his girlfriend borrowed on a Hualien coast trip and finds that all twenty-four frames have the tip of her thumb in the corner, and he asks the lab to print them all

tracks.title: 京胡的音準
tracks.subject: a piano tuner called to an opera troupe's practice room finds the upright piano tuned to A 440 while the jinghu player insists on a lower pitch, so the two argue and finally meet in the middle

tracks.title: 四十七號掛在我手裡
tracks.subject: a cloakroom girl at a Shanghai-style hotel ballroom keeps hanging the same man's coat on hook number 47, because he keeps losing his ticket on purpose to stay and chat

tracks.title: Carrot Nose
tracks.subject: A girl builds a snowman in the park at lunchtime and ties her crush's lost red scarf on it, hoping he walks past and recognises it

tracks.title: Ticket Number Forty-One
tracks.subject: A man pawns his guitar to buy his wife a ring, and the pawnbroker lets him play it every Sunday before the shop opens

tracks.title: Shoe the Horse
tracks.subject: A Midrand farrier can only fit a cart-horse's new shoes while a slow house track plays, because the old horse stamps in time and stands still

tracks.title: Gold Leaf Mistake
tracks.subject: A shop-front sign-writer gilds the name of a new bakery in gold leaf, spells it wrong, and the owner keeps it because queues form to point at it

tracks.title: The Friday Key
tracks.subject: A woman who has wound the town-hall clock every Friday for thirty years is handed a quartz replacement and asks to wind it one last time with the new mayor

tracks.title: Cincin Longgar
tracks.subject: a young goldsmith in a Pasar Atom Surabaya stall who resizes the same engagement ring three times because the customer's girlfriend's finger swells in the heat, until the man asks him to make it one size loose so it can stay on through every season

tracks.title: Angsa Es
tracks.subject: a hotel ice sculptor in Bandung who carves a swan for the breakfast buffet each dawn, watches it drip away by noon, and finally carves a swan small enough to melt in the palm of the pastry girl he loves

tracks.title: Titik Kumpul
tracks.subject: a volunteer fire warden in a Glodok electronics mall in an orange vest and helmet who shoos three hundred stall owners out in the monthly drill, and at the assembly point finds the phone-case girl counting heads and saying one person is still missing: him

tracks.title: Tabung Melon
tracks.subject: a 3-kilo gas cylinder deliveryman in a Bekasi rusun who carries one up four flights on his shoulder, paid in coins by every tenant and given tea by an old lady on the fourth floor, counting his steps like dance steps

tracks.title: Angka di Meteran
tracks.subject: a PLN electricity meter reader in a Malang lane who reads each household's life in its monthly numbers, and one month a long-silent house jumps overnight and he knocks to find the son who has come home

tracks.title: 赤い糸でとじる
tracks.subject: a young bookbinder who hides one stitch of red thread in every notebook he sews for the girl at the neighbouring paper stall, and waits to see which page she finds it on

tracks.title: 左足の十二時
tracks.subject: a station shoe-shine stand owner who notices that every customer's tapping foot on his footrest settles at the same tempo, and starts a Friday dance on his one chair

tracks.title: 目をつぶる観覧車
tracks.subject: a small-town Ferris wheel operator who has promised the hot-dog seller a free ride, and describes the whole town out loud to her all the way up because she keeps her eyes shut the entire time, afraid of heights

tracks.title: 最後のロープウェイ
tracks.subject: a cable-car operator on a mountain line who announces each station and notices that one woman rides up and down all day without ever getting off, as if she were avoiding going home

tracks.title: パンの手紙
tracks.subject: a young bread delivery boy on a moped who finds a folded love note tucked into one baguette bag that the baker's daughter hid there, with no name and forty balconies to guess from

tracks.title: 검댕 묻은 손도장
tracks.subject: a chimney sweep who clears the ondol flue of one hanok every spring and gets a plate of mugwort rice cake on the step from the daughter of the house

tracks.title: 낙서 금지 토끼
tracks.subject: a wall painter who rolls NO GRAFFITI onto an alley wall every dawn and finds a chalk rabbit beside it each night, until he catches the schoolboy and paints the carrot himself

tracks.title: 깎다 만 연필
tracks.subject: a shy man in a tea house who keeps sharpening one pencil with a pocketknife to avoid writing the first line of a letter to the woman who pours his tea

tracks.title: 해시계 여섯 시
tracks.subject: a man who built a plywood sundial on his rooftop with a painted line for six o'clock and secretly drew the line twenty minutes early so his girlfriend is never late

tracks.title: 깜박이는 가로등 목요일
tracks.subject: a street-lamp repair worker on a lift truck who leaves one lamp flickering on purpose so a girl at a third-floor window keeps lowering a basket of barley tea to him each Thursday

tracks.title: Surat Di Belakang Dail
tracks.genre: Romanian lautari taraf folk dance (hora lenta to sirba)
tracks.subject: a radio repairman in Taiping opens an old Philips valve radio and finds a 1974 love letter behind the dial, then spends the evening tracing its owner by the shop stamp on the back

tracks.title: Burung Pesan Teh Tarik
tracks.subject: a murai bird hung at a kopitiam hook each morning copies the kettle whistle and the aunty's 'teh tarik satu', and now customers order from the bird

tracks.title: Labuh Gaun Dia
tracks.subject: a dressmaker pins the hem of his fiancée's wedding gown on his knees while she insists on wearing sneakers underneath, so he lets the hem change at every fitting

tracks.title: Empat Minit Lambat
tracks.subject: a municipal clock winder in Taiping climbs the tower every Sunday and keeps the clock four minutes slow, the time his wife takes to wave from the window

tracks.title: Empat Ulas Satu Durian
tracks.genre: barbershop quartet (four-part a cappella harmony, tags and swipes)
tracks.subject: four office mates split a single durian from a roadside stall and argue over who gets the biggest pod

tracks.title: 斷線的風吹 Tn̄g-suànn ê Hong-tshue
tracks.subject: A Tamsui kite maker whose Saturday customer keeps coming back to buy the same red-tailed butterfly kite, always 'lost' with the string cut clean as if by scissors, until she hides her phone number on the tail and he comes in empty-handed to invite her to the riverbank.

tracks.title: 上尾一格 Siōng-bué Tsi̍t-keh
tracks.mood: tender, tongue-tied, relieved at the last second
tracks.subject: A husband who stormed out over selling the old rattan chair stands at the last card-phone booth outside Tainan station with a dead mobile and one unit left on his phone card, dials the only number he remembers, cannot speak, and hears her tell him not to hang up.

tracks.title: 冰角內底的批 Ping-kak Lāi-té ê Phue
tracks.subject: A woman at a Tonggang ice factory slips a sealed one-line note into each tank before the 24-hour freeze so it sits inside the block loaded on her husband's boat, and when he comes home he returns the whole bundle of salt-stained notes with a pencil reply on the last one.

tracks.title: 等彼班車 Tán Hit Pan Tshia
tracks.subject: A 70-year-old hand-cranked level-crossing keeper on a Huwei sugar railway lowers the barrier at 3:15 for the one slow tourist train a day, and has waited eleven years beside the same woman on a scooter without asking her name, until the day the train is cancelled and neither of them leaves.

tracks.title: 三个零 Sann-ê Lîng
tracks.subject: A woman crouched at a Taichung station bicycle rack cannot recall her three-digit lock code, tries her birthday, her mother's and a stranger's, a crowd gathers with guesses, and a child finally tries 000, the factory setting she never changed.

tracks.title: เห็ดดอกเดียวบนเนินเขา
tracks.genre: Thai highland Tibetan-style pop (dranyen and flute)
tracks.subject: Before dawn after the first rain on a hillside near Chiang Mai, forager Kaew and old Lung Boon grab the same giant mushroom at once, refuse to let go, then split it and boil it into soup on a stone fire.

tracks.title: ผีประจำตู้เจ็ด
tracks.subject: A scare actor at a Bangkok amusement-park ghost train who must leap out at car seven finds the same girl riding alone every Saturday, and today she waves at him and says hello, so he forgets his lines.

tracks.title: เชือกยาวสิบวา
tracks.genre: Argentine-style chacarera folk (6/8, guitar and bombo legüero)
tracks.mood: warm, teasing, quietly romantic dance feel
tracks.subject: A young hemp rope-maker in a riverside yard in Ayutthaya, walking backwards as he twists the strands, gets an order from a boat girl for a ten-wa rope to hang a hammock for two between two mango trees, and twists it slowly so she must come back.

tracks.title: ชื่อเธอใต้ป้ายแหวน
tracks.genre: 1980s power ballad AOR (big drums, synth pad, guitar solo)
tracks.subject: At 2 a.m. on a scaffold above a Bangkok Skytrain line, a billboard paster glues the giant panels of a diamond-ring advert and secretly writes his girlfriend's name and a proposal in the last corner, knowing she passes it at 8:10 every morning.

tracks.title: ไซริมห้วยของใคร
tracks.genre: Hill-tribe folk-pop (Karen/Akha style, bamboo flute and group chant)
tracks.subject: A young hill-village man checks his bamboo fish trap by the stream every morning and finds his fish swapped for wild bananas, then a flower, and follows small footprints in the mud to the headman's daughter by the footbridge.

tracks.title: Chữ A Nhảy Dòng
tracks.genre: tân cổ giao duyên dance-pop (cải lương-pop)
tracks.subject: A young woman brings her late grandfather's Olympia typewriter to a Sài Gòn repair stall on Lê Công Kiều; the old repairman fixes everything except the letter A that jumps a line, and she keeps coming back on Saturdays, until she realises he leaves it unfixed on purpose so she keeps visiting.

tracks.title: Thư Rơi Vào Hộp
tracks.subject: A girl posts a love letter into a red street mailbox on Hàng Bông and one minute later regrets it, so she waits at the box until the postman comes at four; he cannot hand letters back, but he lets her read the addresses on the pile, and she finds the boy's letter to her has been in the box just as long.

tracks.title: Vẽ Tai Anh To Hơn
tracks.genre: Khmer 1960s garage-psych rock sung in Vietnamese
tracks.subject: A street caricaturist on the pavement beside Hồ Hoàn Kiếm gets a customer who pays to have his girlfriend drawn, and she asks him to enlarge the boyfriend's ears instead; the drawing is so ridiculous the boyfriend carries it home, frames it, and finally asks her to marry him.

tracks.title: Ô Chữ Số Bảy Ngang
tracks.genre: Filipino Manila sound (1970s orchestral pop) sung in Vietnamese
tracks.subject: A young newspaper delivery boy in Huế drops the paper at the same second-floor flat every morning and notices the crossword left half-filled on the table; one day he fills in seven across, and a reply in her handwriting waits the next morning, until the crossword becomes their only conversation and they finally meet at the door.

tracks.title: Số Điện Đứng Yên
tracks.genre: French chanson réaliste sung in Vietnamese
tracks.subject: A meter reader on a Hải Phòng back street reads the same widow's electricity meter every month and notices that the figure has stood still for three months; she has been living by candlelight since her husband's old lamp broke, and he starts leaving new bulbs on the step with the monthly reading slip, until she turns the lamp on again.

tracks.title: 斜住嘅城市
tracks.subject: A Peak Tram driver who has tilted the whole of Central sideways for twenty years buys one egg tart a day from the girl at the lower-terminal kiosk and never says more, until on the steepest stretch he presses the wrong button, the announcement mic goes live, and he asks her out in front of two hundred passengers.

tracks.title: 三米高
tracks.subject: A stilt walker working the Tsim Sha Tsui promenade at three metres tall can see every rooftop water tank in Kowloon but cannot bend down, so when a tourist toddler's coin bounces out of his hat onto the paving it takes a small girl climbing onto a bench to hand it back.

tracks.title: 三分四十秒
tracks.subject: A Sham Shui Po candle maker is asked by a young man for one taper that burns exactly three minutes forty seconds, the length of the song he will propose to, and spends the night dipping and timing twelve test candles with a stopwatch until the thirteenth is right.

tracks.title: 收低張紙
tracks.subject: A flyer-hander outside Mong Kok station has been refused eleven thousand times in six years and is about to give up when an old lady takes the leaflet, reads the whole thing aloud in the street, and gets a crowd to queue for the free tea at a shop that turns out to be closed.

tracks.title: 多停三秒
tracks.subject: A Central observation-wheel operator who holds the wheel still for three extra seconds at the top for an old woman who rides alone every Tuesday to look at the old Star Ferry pier where she once worked as a typist, and who one Tuesday asks the operator why he never rides himself.

tracks.title: 兩個名字刻一顆
tracks.genre: Inner Mongolian long-song (urtiin duu) style ballad with tovshuur and limbe
tracks.subject: a stone name-seal carver in a lane workshop whose young couple customers cannot agree on a name for their baby, so he carves one name on each end of the same stone and tells them to press both

tracks.title: 三分鐘的側臉
tracks.subject: a street paper-cutting artist who cuts silhouette portraits in three minutes, and the man who cannot stop smiling while he sits still, so the paper face comes out grinning and she keeps it

tracks.title: 車掌今天不重複
tracks.subject: a city bus conductor with a punch pliers who calls every stop in a brand-new rhyme and never repeats one, while the regulars secretly keep a tally to bet he cannot last a whole day

tracks.title: 三年前的那只鐘
tracks.genre: Quebec chanson with accordion and upright bass (Mandarin storytelling)
tracks.subject: a clock repairer whose window is lined with fixed clocks nobody collected, and the woman who comes to pick hers up three years late and is told she is only three years behind

tracks.title: 白手套的路口
tracks.genre: Levantine dabke folk-pop with mijwiz, oud and tabla
tracks.subject: a traffic officer in white gloves at a busy crossroads whose hand signals start to follow a stomping beat, until pedestrians, delivery riders and a bus driver fall into step and the whole crossing moves in a line

tracks.title: Table Four, Table Six
tracks.subject: On a blind date set up by his sister, Colin sits at table four and Jan at table six of a Liverpool tea room, each secretly brought a best friend to spy from the next table, and it is the two spies who start talking.

tracks.title: The Penny Blue
tracks.subject: A woman goes to the Saturday stamp fair in a church hall to buy one gift, keeps returning to the same dealer's table asking for the penny blue, and is really watching his careful tweezers.

tracks.title: Floor Thirty-One
tracks.subject: A Lagos high-rise window cleaner on a rope seat watches a man on floor thirty-one rehearse his resignation speech to the glass every Tuesday, nods him on, and the man finally quits and waves the cleaner in for coffee.

tracks.title: Six Ten at the Swing Bridge
tracks.subject: A swing-bridge keeper on a small river turns the span open at 6:10 every morning for one coal barge, knows its pilot only by her two horn blasts and a lamp, and today leaves the bridge open and walks down to the quay with two cups of tea.

tracks.title: Greensleeves on Every Street
tracks.subject: An ice-cream van driver whose chime box is jammed on four bars of one tune sells out on every estate because children chase it, and decides to build his whole route around it.

tracks.title: Empat Puluh Persen
tracks.subject: a Medan radio weather forecaster who every morning is phoned by listeners asking which forty percent of the city will get the rain, until he starts answering street by street

tracks.title: Sepatu Sekolah Ukuran Besar
tracks.subject: a shoe cobbler at a Kupang market who stitches a boy's school shoes with fishing line each term and secretly keeps the next size up on the shelf for him

tracks.title: Satu Dua Cha-cha-cha
tracks.subject: a 58-year-old man with two left feet who secretly pays for ten ballroom lessons so he can dance one proper cha-cha with his wife on their thirtieth anniversary

tracks.title: Telapak Tanganku Kosong
tracks.subject: a palm reader at a Yogyakarta night fair who tells every customer a bright future, and has never dared to read his own palm

tracks.title: Jendela Seberang
tracks.subject: a tower crane operator in Jakarta who sits forty metres up every morning and sees a woman across the street water her windowsill herbs, and finally lowers his hook with a note

tracks.title: しっぽの人
tracks.subject: the rear-end operator inside a two-person wooden horse puppet at a children's theatre, who has seen only his front partner's back for twelve years and must learn to follow a new girl when the old partner is out

tracks.title: 手首の買い物メモ
tracks.subject: a husband in a tattoo studio on their tenth anniversary having his wife's fridge shopping note, ending with 'love you' in her handwriting, inked on his wrist while the tattooist says people usually pick a name

tracks.title: 半音ずれたラ
tracks.subject: a piano tuner at an old couple's house whose upright has one A key slightly flat; the husband has played the same wrong note for forty years and the wife asks him to leave it exactly as it is

tracks.title: 壁を三回
tracks.subject: the woman who stokes the wood-fired boiler behind a small public bathhouse, who for twenty years has been answering a regular customer's knocks on the wall (two taps too hot, one tap just right) until tonight he knocks three times

tracks.title: サインのれんしゅう
tracks.subject: a stationery-shop clerk who has to swap the test-pad every week because one customer fills it with the same signature practised over and over, until he explains he took his wife's surname when they married

tracks.title: 빨간 펜 한 자루
tracks.subject: a freelance proofreader who walks the town at dusk and fixes typos on cloth shop banners with a red marker, until the bakery owner whose banner he corrected catches him and hands him a loaf

tracks.title: 같은 이름을 부르면
tracks.subject: two strangers both named Kim Jiyoung stand up when a hospital waiting room calls the name, swap their prescription envelopes by mistake, and meet again to swap them back

tracks.title: 빨래집게 하나
tracks.subject: a woman hanging washing on her rooftop line finds one clothespin missing every Sunday, discovers a crow is taking them for its nest, and starts leaving spare pins on the wall

tracks.title: 본관이 어디세요
tracks.subject: two coworkers named Kim at a clan reunion picnic find out they come from different ancestral seats, Gimhae and Gyeongju, and he says out loud that this means he is free to ask her out

tracks.title: 분필로 그은 눈금
tracks.genre: Andean folk-pop with quena and charango
tracks.subject: a woman who walks a neighbourhood stream each morning and marks the water level on the concrete wall with chalk, until a small boy starts copying her marks beside hers

tracks.title: Simpulan Terakhir
tracks.genre: Malay Neapolitan tarantella-pop (mandolin-and-accordion fast 6/8 folk dance)
tracks.subject: a children's-party magician who has pulled the same chain of silk scarves from his sleeve for twenty-five years, and tonight his wife-assistant finds a ring knotted in the last scarf, the ring he could not afford at their wedding

tracks.title: Tangan Kiri Bawah Meja
tracks.genre: Malay calypso (Caribbean steel-pan calypso with Malay comic storytelling)
tracks.subject: a left-handed man at his girlfriend's mother's first Sunday lunch, forcing himself to eat nasi with his right hand while his left hides under the table, until the mother hands him the sambal with her own left hand and winks

tracks.title: Kad Kecil
tracks.genre: Malay gamelan Melayu pop ballad (Terengganu/Pahang court-gamelan colour)
tracks.subject: a florist who writes the card for tongue-tied men, and the shy regular who every Friday dictates a different card for one name, Aini, her own name, until he stops asking her to deliver it

tracks.title: Pisau Setengah Jari
tracks.genre: Malay spaghetti-western cinematic ballad (Morricone-style desert-circus soundtrack)
tracks.subject: a circus knife-thrower's wife who stands against the wooden board every night as his target, the knife that lands half a finger from her ear tonight, and her dry verdict that he is getting better

tracks.title: Cadar Sarung
tracks.subject: a couple trying to put a fitted sheet on a bed on Saturday morning, fighting over which corner is which and finally meeting in the middle of the mattress

tracks.title: 加一个岫 Ke Tsi̍t Ê Siū
tracks.subject: A Wanhua rooftop pigeon keeper whose grey hen keeps coming home with the same unringed stray cock, so he grumbles, nails up a second box and scatters extra grain.

tracks.title: 鞋帶鬆去矣 Ê-tuà Sang Khì Ah
tracks.subject: A nine-year-old who already knows how to tie laces but keeps loosening them so the sixth-grade crossing guard with the yellow flag will kneel and re-tie them each morning, until she says she knew all along and just wanted a rest.

tracks.title: 毋看鏡頭 M̄ Khuànn Kèng-thâu
tracks.subject: In a bridal-photo studio's second-floor set the groom looks at the bride instead of the lens in all forty shots; the photographer sighs, the make-up artist retouches again, and she decides to keep that look.

tracks.title: 輪仔內底的戒指 Lián-á Lāi-té ê Kài-tsí
tracks.subject: A Pingtung roadside tyre-repair man finds a gold ring wedged in the tread of a scooter tyre and holds it up at the red light for every passing rider, until a delivery woman who lost it a week ago stops; she says she had already bought a new one but still wants this one.

tracks.title: 一指寬 Tsi̍t Tsí Khuann
tracks.subject: A woman at a department-store basement alteration counter whom the same bespectacled man visits every week to shorten the same trousers one finger, then let them down again, until she asks whether he is measuring the hem or her.

tracks.title: ตีสี่กับหุ่นโชว์
tracks.genre: Thai Congolese soukous (rumba-derived guitar dance song)
tracks.subject: At 4 a.m. before a Siam department store opens, window dresser Noi pins a sequinned lime-green dress onto a stubborn mannequin, ends up swaying her around the display to fix the fit, and the manager walks in early.

tracks.title: ฟันบนอยู่ใต้ถุน
tracks.subject: Seven-year-old Prae throws her fallen upper tooth under her grandmother's stilt house, as custom says, then crawls under with her father's torch and finds a marble, an earring and grandpa's whistle but no tooth, while the hen eyes her.

tracks.title: สี่นาทีของลุงสม
tracks.genre: Thai ranat ek and string quartet chamber pop
tracks.subject: Uncle Som, keeper of a provincial clock tower in Phrae, climbs sixty-one steps each Sunday to wind it and sets it four minutes fast on purpose so the rushing townsfolk arrive on time, and he hides the key when the district office orders it corrected.

tracks.title: ทอนเจ็ดสิบห้า
tracks.genre: Thai 1960s Italian canzone pop (Sanremo-style strings and mandolin)
tracks.subject: Mon, a toll-booth attendant at lane three of a Bangkok expressway, has three seconds a day with the woman in the white car who always pays exact coins; the day she hands him a 100-baht note, he counts the 75 baht change slowly while she smiles and horns sound behind.

tracks.title: ร้อยสี่สิบสามแผ่น
tracks.genre: Thai choir-led gospel-soul with piano and hand claps
tracks.subject: A first-time father pacing outside a delivery room counts 143 ceiling tiles, clutching tiny socks he bought in May, until the nurse leaves the door ajar and he hears the first cry and sits down on the floor.

tracks.title: Cuộn Len Thứ Mười Một
tracks.subject: A shy young man in a Đà Lạt wool shop is asked to hold a skein of yarn across both hands while a girl winds it into a ball; twenty minutes of facing her undoes him, so he buys a skein every Saturday, owns eleven, cannot knit, and finally lets her teach him the first stitch.

tracks.title: Tấm Vé Bằng Sáp Màu
tracks.subject: Chú Lực, a strict ticket inspector on Hà Nội's Cát Linh metro, finds a six-year-old boy riding every morning with a ticket drawn in crayon; he stamps it as valid day after day, until the station chief comes down to inspect and Chú Lực has to defend a drawing.

tracks.title: Cuốn Sổ Ba Mươi Mốt Tên
tracks.subject: Bà Sáu, godmother to thirty-one children of her Biên Hòa parish, has never missed one godchild's birthday, each logged in a school notebook; on her own eightieth birthday, an ordinary Sunday after mass, she has forgotten it, and all thirty-one godchildren are waiting at the church gate with a brass band and presents.

tracks.title: Loa Bến Xe Số Mười Hai
tracks.subject: Chị Hương, the loudspeaker announcer at a coach station, sings out each departure in the same cadence; coach driver Tài has rolled out on her last word for three years, and the day she swaps in a new line he stalls the engine on the platform, and the whole station hears her laugh.

tracks.title: Dấu Hỏi Dấu Ngã
tracks.genre: Vietnamese ru con-style folk lullaby ballad
tracks.subject: A café owner writes her chalkboard menu every dawn and keeps putting the wrong tone mark on words, 'sửa' for 'sữa'; each morning a stranger quietly rubs out the wrong mark with his thumb and fixes it, so she starts making the mistakes on purpose, until one morning the board is corrected and signed.

tracks.title: 最後一題
tracks.subject: A Wednesday-night host of a small local TV quiz in a Tseung Kwan O studio flips over the final-round card and finds it blank, so he asks the first thing in his head, whether the contestant has eaten yet, and a 70-year-old grandmother buzzes first and wins the restaurant voucher.

tracks.title: 吹哨輝叔
tracks.subject: A 68-year-old retired storeroom clerk, Uncle Fai, gets new dentures that whistle on every four and every ten he says, so his wife can hear him coming from two streets away and finally catches him sneaking barbecue pork buns.

tracks.title: 畢業冊後頁
tracks.subject: A man pulls out his 1999 school yearbook after twenty-five years, finds a pencilled phone number on the back page that says call me after the exams, and dials it; the voice that answers says she had been wondering when he would look.

tracks.title: 十二樓B座
tracks.subject: A flower shop delivery woman rings flat 12B every Friday for a bouquet meant for 12D, and the lonely man in 12B, who has never received flowers, keeps taking them without correcting her until he leaves a thank-you note.

tracks.title: 一隻玻璃碟
tracks.subject: A woman finally returns a glass casserole dish with her friend's name on masking tape on the bottom, borrowed nineteen years ago when soup was brought after her baby was born, and stands holding it outside her friend's old door.

tracks.title: 掌紋接上了
tracks.subject: a young woman who reads palms at a night-market folding table, a trade her grandfather taught her, and the man who sits down, asks no question about money or exams, and whose palm lines meet hers exactly when they touch

tracks.title: 磨到剩一片柳葉
tracks.subject: a hotel kitchen apprentice who inherits the retired chef's thirty-year-old cleaver, worn narrow as a willow leaf, resists changing its shape on the whetstone, and finds the handle already dented to fit his thumb

tracks.title: 黃旗搖搖過馬路
tracks.subject: a retired volunteer crossing guard at a Tainan primary-school corner waving his big yellow flag at 7:20 each morning, and the day he is five minutes late and the children stop the traffic with his flag themselves

tracks.title: 水桶裡找洞
tracks.subject: a bicycle-shop mender who dunks inner tubes in a water bucket to find the leak by its bubbles, and the young man who comes back every afternoon at 4:30 with a tyre that has no puncture at all, on a bike he rents by the hour just to stand by her bucket

tracks.title: 多撥一顆珠
tracks.subject: a stationery-shop abacus teacher in her sixties whose Saturday class gets one retired vegetable seller, who gets every sum wrong by exactly one bead so that she has to lean over to fix it, and the day he finally gets one right

tracks.title: I Only Know Your Eyes
tracks.subject: Two day-shift packers on a biscuit factory's custard-cream line fall in love knowing only each other's eyes between hairnet and blue beard snood, and outside the gate she walks straight past him until he cups his hands over his beard.

tracks.title: Eleven Elections
tracks.subject: Two poll clerks share a trestle table in a village hall only on election days, eleven in twenty years, until she catches herself hoping for a snap election and, as the box is sealed at ten, he asks why wait for the next.

tracks.title: Run, Hank, Run
tracks.subject: A wife on the Ocmulgee riverbank in Macon watches a gust lift her husband's auburn toupee off his head and a neighbour's coonhound trot off with it, and has to decide whether to admit she has known since the wedding day.

tracks.title: I Only Asked About the Fountain
tracks.subject: A man new to town goes to his first residents' association AGM only to ask why the square's fountain has been dry since 2016, raises his hand at the wrong moment, and walks home elected treasurer, carrying a biscuit tin with £41.17 in it.

tracks.title: Nana's Got an Anchor
tracks.subject: A grandmother who has never been to sea gets an anchor tattooed on her forearm for her seventieth birthday and hides it under cardigans all summer from her disapproving daughter, who finally rolls up her own sleeve to show a swallow hidden since 1996.

tracks.title: Sabun Kecil dari Tiap Kota
tracks.mood: hangat, sabar, rindu yang tenang (warm, patient, quietly missing him)
tracks.subject: In their first rented house in Sidoarjo, a wife lines the bathroom shelf with the hotel soaps her husband, a travelling generator technician, brings home from every town, reads his month from the wrappers, and never unwraps the one from their honeymoon in Batu.

tracks.title: Kursi Tiga A
tracks.subject: On his first flight as co-pilot, a young Garuda pilot from Padang makes the cabin announcement and hears his own mother in seat 3A answer back, with fourteen relatives filling rows three to seven waving at the cockpit door.

tracks.title: Inyong Ora Gugup
tracks.subject: A Purwokerto graduate in a Jakarta job interview keeps her standard Indonesian polished until the interviewer slips, and he turns out to be from Cilacap, so she answers in ngapak and both of them laugh.

tracks.title: Turang, Geser Dulu
tracks.mood: riang, menggoda, bergoyang (cheerful, teasing, made for dancing)
tracks.subject: At a Kabanjahe kerja tahun, a Karo boy and his cousin turang, who by custom must open the landek together, plot to swap partners so each can dance with the person he or she actually likes.

tracks.title: Titik Akhir
tracks.subject: Two first-year chemistry students share one burette in a Pekanbaru campus lab; he keeps overshooting the endpoint to dark pink because he watches her instead of the drops, the assistant makes them start over until dusk, and she steadies his hand on the tap.

tracks.title: 竜の目はまだ
tracks.subject: A shy accounting clerk who hand-embroiders a dragon on the back of a plain black jacket at his low table every night, one scale an evening, and keeps leaving the eye unstitched because a finished jacket would have to be worn outside.

tracks.title: ノーガター・ブギ
tracks.subject: Two forty-year-old friends who have rolled nothing but gutter balls since high school ask a Showa-era bowling alley to raise the kids' bumper rails for a nephew who does not exist, and are handed the dinosaur ball ramp too.

tracks.title: Kが打てない
tracks.subject: A woman who types her boyfriend Keisuke a romaji note every morning on a flea-market typewriter whose K key has died, so she cannot write 'suki' or even his name and ends up typing 'aishiteru' for the first time.

tracks.title: ハーフサイズのふたり
tracks.subject: A couple who share one old half-frame camera on Sunday walks round the park pond, taking turns to photograph each other, and when the seventy-two-shot roll finally comes back months later, two frames to a print, they are side by side in every one.

tracks.title: メダル四万枚グランドレビュー
tracks.genre: Japanese revue show tune (Osaka all-female revue style)
tracks.subject: Yoshie, seventy-four, who has forty thousand medals banked at a game centre above an Osaka supermarket, worthless anywhere else and wiped if she stays away sixty days, so she clocks in at the coin pusher daily and tips kids a cupful like candy.

tracks.title: 패딩 좀 들어 줘
tracks.mood: pent-up and deadpan in the verses, then a jump-until-closing release in the fast chorus
tracks.subject: Jiwoo, 96% 'I' on every MBTI test, is dragged to a Hongdae club by three 'E' friends and stands at the wall holding four padded coats, until her song drops at 1 a.m.; she hands the coats over and out-jumps them all until closing.

tracks.title: 콩이 은퇴식
tracks.mood: mock-solemn, deadpan-comic, strutting; proud affection under the drama
tracks.subject: Told by her handler: at Gimhae Airport the retirement send-off for Kongi, an eight-year-old quarantine detector beagle, goes smoothly until she trots off the podium mid-speech and sits, her trained alert, in front of the director's briefcase, where a snack sausage is hidden.

tracks.title: 바꿔 뿌려 봐
tracks.mood: playful, teasing, cosy; warm banter that ends in laughing relief
tracks.subject: For a year Sohee has held her breath in the heavy rose perfume Minjun gave her, while he dutifully wears the leathery cologne she picked and secretly hates; at their second-anniversary dinner both confess, swap bottles, and each scent suits its giver.

tracks.title: 한 개 더
tracks.mood: tender, shy and bright, like an 80s idol ballad-pop song (an ordinary Wednesday closing time)
tracks.subject: Sung by a 19-year-old part-timer at a Sinchon donut counter: every Wednesday ten minutes before closing a tired man buys one plain glazed and eats it standing; this week she has read his birthday off his points card and slips a second, pink-sprinkle donut into his box.

tracks.title: 핑크 반장
tracks.mood: mock-heroic, proud, soft-hearted under the pomp
tracks.subject: Rebar foreman Mr Bae's six-year-old daughter paints his nails bright pink on Sunday night and makes him promise not to wipe it off, so he runs Monday's 7 a.m. safety briefing bare-handed, and by Friday every man on his crew has one pink pinky.

tracks.title: Kamek Sayang Kitak
tracks.subject: At the Kuching Waterfront over two glasses of teh C peng, a Sarawakian woman tells her Kedah boyfriend 'kamek sayang kitak'; he hears 'kami sayang kita', asks who 'we' are, and once she translates answers in his own dialect: 'aku sayang hang'.

tracks.title: Kambing Rembau
tracks.genre: Malay cumbia (Colombian cumbia rhythm with Malay folk spirit)
tracks.subject: Abang Usop, a mason who usually builds drains and bus stops in Rembau, gets three weeks to make the town's cement buffalo monument; at the unveiling a child shouts 'kambing!', the name sticks, and the lopsided 'goat' becomes the town's proudest landmark.

tracks.title: Dam Haji Seorang
tracks.mood: wry, lonesome, warming to a smile
tracks.subject: Since his dam haji opponent moved to Johor Bahru, 71-year-old Mat Zin has played both sides with bottle caps against an empty stool under a mango tree in Lenggong, until the young Bangladeshi pump attendant from across the road sits down and beats him.

tracks.title: Angsana Hujung Lorong
tracks.subject: Every night Hazwan walks Najwa home past the old angsana tree at the end of her lorong said to hold a pontianak, insisting it is to protect her; she hums so he thinks she is brave while his sweating hand grips hers, and one night she turns round and walks him home instead.

tracks.title: Alih Suara Pak Long
tracks.subject: Outside Soon Huat's electrical shop in Muar, retired lorry driver Pak Long dubs a muted Turkish drama on twelve display TVs for the pavement crowd, inventing every line, until the owner's daughter turns on sound and subtitles and everyone begs her to mute it again.

tracks.title: 五台車一个聲 Gōo Tâi Tshia Tsi̍t Ê Siann
tracks.subject: The auntie who records sound-truck slogans behind a Huwei stationery shop voices all five rival council candidates (numbers only, no real parties), so in the final week her own voice out-shouts itself at the roundabout, and she still won't tell her husband her vote.

tracks.title: 上尾彼个名 Siōng-bué Hit Ê Miâ
